**Continuity:** K-GUIDE · K-STATE · K-EVD · K-VIEW. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-ASTRA, SRC-RECON, SRC-POLYIA96.

### PIA-042 · IV.06 — Production capture

**Mandate.** PRODUCE captures actual artifact bytes, paths, versions and semantic scope. Preserve immutable snapshots even if a working file later changes. Show workspace drift separately, and require explicit re-production for a new candidate.

**Acceptance.** Produce/reopen tests resolve the original bytes; editing the workspace does not alter captured evidence and cannot silently certify the changed file.

**Continuity:** K-GUIDE · K-STATE · K-EVD · K-VIEW. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-ASTRA, SRC-RECON, SRC-POLYIA96.

### PIA-043 · IV.07 — Verification execution

**Mandate.** VERIFY invokes a registered trusted verifier with declared inputs, source identity and evidence class. The caller cannot supply a pass flag, substitute a hash-looking string or bypass scientific checks with file existence. A failed verifier remains visible and blocks acceptance.

**Acceptance.** Forged evidence, unknown verifiers, tampered artifacts and explicit failing checks all refuse acceptance; successful receipts bind actual verifier code and inputs.

**Continuity:** K-GUIDE · K-STATE · K-EVD · K-VIEW. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-ASTRA, SRC-RECON, SRC-POLYIA96.

### PIA-044 · IV.08 — Acceptance and supersession

**Mandate.** ACCEPT applies only to the verified artifact version and its exact obligations. Later production invalidates the candidate's previous verification while retaining historical accepted snapshots. Whole-mission acceptance is a separate conjunction of required gates.

**Acceptance.** A re-produced artifact cannot inherit acceptance automatically; accepting the bootstrap cannot change the full mission to commissioned.

**Continuity:** K-GUIDE · K-STATE · K-EVD · K-VIEW. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-ASTRA, SRC-RECON, SRC-POLYIA96.

### PIA-045 · IV.09 — DODGE work contracts

**Mandate.** Every work item has Deliverable, Obligations, Dependencies, Guards and Evidence. This package's DODGE label is a house organizational convention. It links expected outputs and definitions of done without forcing Codex to follow arbitrary calendar phases.

**Acceptance.** Machine registry validates all five fields, dependency references and evidence requirements; UI displays dependency-ready and blocked work intelligibly.

**Continuity:** K-GUIDE · K-STATE · K-EVD · K-VIEW. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-ASTRA, SRC-RECON, SRC-POLYIA96.

### PIA-046 · IV.10 — Refusal and diagnostic custody

**Mandate.** Retain refusal reason, attempted kind, actor scope, expected/current revision and safe diagnostics separately from accepted transitions. Redact credentials and private payloads according to policy. A refusal is useful evidence, not an unreported exception.

**Acceptance.** Negative controls are queryable; authentication failures reveal no state or tokens; unsupported command paths have stable error codes.

**Continuity:** K-GUIDE · K-STATE · K-EVD · K-VIEW. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-ASTRA, SRC-RECON, SRC-POLYIA96.

### PIA-047 · IV.11 — Human-readable workbench

**Mandate.** Provide a real working interface for state, obligations, sources, produced artifacts, verification outcomes, guidance, experiments, checkpoints and blockers. Use actual service data, honest connection indicators and accessible controls. Keep implementation jargon out of explanations where it does not help a decision.

**Acceptance.** A human can complete submit/ack/apply and produce/verify/accept workflows through the UI and see the same receipts as an API client.

**Continuity:** K-GUIDE · K-STATE · K-EVD · K-VIEW. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-ASTRA, SRC-RECON, SRC-POLYIA96.

### PIA-048 · IV.12 — Progress without narrative dependence

**Mandate.** Each checkpoint exports a concise STATUS, NEXT_STATE, source lock, capability index, obligation/evidence matrix, negative results and cost report. These are projections of machine state and immutable receipts, not independently edited claims of success.

**Acceptance.** A new Codex or observer reconstructs completed, active and blocked work from the URL or repository export, with no need for the prior chat transcript.

**Continuity:** K-GUIDE · K-STATE · K-EVD · K-VIEW. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-ASTRA, SRC-RECON, SRC-POLYIA96.

## Title V — Forms, alphabets, grammars and semantics

### PIA-049 · V.01 — Formal vocabulary

**Mandate.** Define symbol, token, letter, alphabet, word, expression, grammar, interpretation, value, type, operator, state, transition, machine, model, theorem and witness with distinct identities. Preserve source-specific senses through namespaces and aliases. The same spelling may name different mathematical structures.

**Acceptance.** Vocabulary schema records established/house status, source anchors, examples and non-examples; ambiguous terms resolve to alternatives rather than silent conflation.

**Continuity:** K-SEM · K-GEN · K-LANG. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCGFOUNDATIONS, SRC-UCG156, SRC-PLICA, SRC-GRAMMATONOMIA.

### PIA-050 · V.02 — Typed alphabets

**Mandate.** An alphabet is a declared family of typed generators with identity, admissibility and coordinates/relations where relevant. Support finite enumerations and effective generators, including lettered, numeric, geometric, graph-indexed, phonetic and product forms. An organizational table is an alphabet representation only under an explicit interpretation.

**Acceptance.** Construct one validated alphabet of each inherited kind, demonstrate a product alphabet and distinguish a periodic-table layout from a chemical generative law.

**Continuity:** K-SEM · K-GEN · K-LANG. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCGFOUNDATIONS, SRC-UCG156, SRC-PLICA, SRC-GRAMMATONOMIA.

### PIA-051 · V.03 — Words and index structures

**Mandate.** Represent a word as a labeling of an explicit finite index structure: sequence, tuple, rooted tree, graph, grid, multiset or cyclic order. Keep index shape and symbol identities separate. State the symmetry/equivalence used to identify representations.

**Acceptance.** Round trips preserve labeled structure; tests distinguish ordered tuples from multisets and graph incidence from a renderer's layout.

**Continuity:** K-SEM · K-GEN · K-LANG. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCGFOUNDATIONS, SRC-UCG156, SRC-PLICA, SRC-GRAMMATONOMIA.

### PIA-052 · V.04 — Grammar interface

**Mandate.** A grammar declares alphabet/signature, admissible constructions, derivation relation, diagnostics, version and applicable decision procedure. Support regular, context-free, tree, graph, attribute and term-rewriting adapters with honest termination/decidability limits. Uniform interfaces do not establish a universal membership algorithm.

**Acceptance.** Positive/negative fixtures cover each supported formalism, and unsupported or resource-limited membership returns an explicit non-proof result.

**Continuity:** K-SEM · K-GEN · K-LANG. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCGFOUNDATIONS, SRC-UCG156, SRC-PLICA, SRC-GRAMMATONOMIA.

### PIA-053 · V.05 — In-grammar and negative forms

**Mandate.** Store scoped prohibited, missing, conflicting, hypothetical and empirically excluded forms with provenance and evidence. In-grammar is not automatically the logical complement of a language and a dataset omission is not impossibility. Negative information participates in planning and explanation.

**Acceptance.** Distinct fixtures produce no-edge-found, forbidden-by-rule, contradicted-by-witness, unresolved and budget-exhausted results without collapsing them.

**Continuity:** K-SEM · K-GEN · K-LANG. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCGFOUNDATIONS, SRC-UCG156, SRC-PLICA, SRC-GRAMMATONOMIA.

### PIA-054 · V.06 — Expression and evaluation

**Mandate.** Parse expressions into typed structure before interpretation. Distinguish syntax, denotation, evaluation strategy and execution effects. Explain f(g(x)), matrix transpose/product and chemical formulae through their declared environments; a short string may denote an expensive operation but is not executable without semantics.

**Acceptance.** Tests validate function-composition order, matrix dimensions and a chemical formula's descriptive role; ambiguous or unbound symbols are refused with context.

**Continuity:** K-SEM · K-GEN · K-LANG. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCGFOUNDATIONS, SRC-UCG156, SRC-PLICA, SRC-GRAMMATONOMIA.

### PIA-055 · V.07 — Denotation and realization

**Mandate.** Every grammar declares a semantic domain and partial interpretation. Admissibility, realizability, computability and affordability are separate properties. H2O encodes composition under a chemical notation contract; it does not by itself specify preparation, geometry or a physical process.

**Acceptance.** Produce examples of valid syntax with undefined denotation, an interpreted object with no admitted executor and a valid but budget-exceeding computation.

**Continuity:** K-SEM · K-GEN · K-LANG. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCGFOUNDATIONS, SRC-UCG156, SRC-PLICA, SRC-GRAMMATONOMIA.

### PIA-056 · V.08 — Equality and equivalence

**Mandate.** Name syntactic equality, canonical-form equality, structural isomorphism, observational equivalence and theorem-level equality separately. Finite numerical agreement is evidence on tested points only. Quotients declare their relation and assumptions before representatives are merged.

**Acceptance.** Tests retain domain exclusions, detect a counterexample outside sampled points and prevent numerical support from being promoted to universal equality.

**Continuity:** K-SEM · K-GEN · K-LANG. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCGFOUNDATIONS, SRC-UCG156, SRC-PLICA, SRC-GRAMMATONOMIA.

### PIA-057 · V.09 — Types, contexts and assumptions

**Mandate.** Every operation carries type, algebraic context, units, domain restrictions, effects and evidence requirements. Context transport is a declared map with preservation/loss obligations. A changed context can yield the same result, so dependency custody cannot rely only on output inequality.

**Acceptance.** Context-sensitive examples record both dependencies even when outputs coincide, and reject incompatible fields, dimensions or authorization contexts.

**Continuity:** K-SEM · K-GEN · K-LANG. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCGFOUNDATIONS, SRC-UCG156, SRC-PLICA, SRC-GRAMMATONOMIA.

### PIA-058 · V.10 — State and variance grammar

**Mandate.** Define state space, event alphabet, transition relation, guards, observations and invariant predicates. A state shift is a typed transition; an observation or rendering change has its own declared effect class. Study trace languages, bisimulation and compositional contracts without assuming every state system is finite.

**Acceptance.** A machine's trace validates against its declared grammar; illegal shifts and semantic mutations disguised as view changes are detected.

**Continuity:** K-SEM · K-GEN · K-LANG. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCGFOUNDATIONS, SRC-UCG156, SRC-PLICA, SRC-GRAMMATONOMIA.

### PIA-059 · V.11 — Charts, transliteration and transport

**Mandate.** Generalize transliteration as a typed representation transport only after defining source/target alphabets, parsing, interpretation, loss and inverse relation. Keep phonetic transliteration, notation conversion, compilation and semantic analogy distinct even when they share a pipeline shape.

**Acceptance.** Chart round trips preserve stated observables or return explicit ambiguity/loss, with one linguistic and one mathematical/software example.

**Continuity:** K-SEM · K-GEN · K-LANG. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCGFOUNDATIONS, SRC-UCG156, SRC-PLICA, SRC-GRAMMATONOMIA.

### PIA-060 · V.12 — Costs as structured semantics

**Mandate.** Record work, space, output size, build/index cost and effect cost relative to a model and input dimensions. O(2) is constant asymptotically; logarithmic and exponential claims require specified functions. Complexity classes and data-structure taxonomies may form alphabets with their own grammars but do not make runtime comparison automatic.

**Acceptance.** Benchmarks state input size, model and overhead; a vocabulary test distinguishes O(1), O(log n), O(n), O(n log n) and O(2^n) with correct examples.

**Continuity:** K-SEM · K-GEN · K-LANG. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCGFOUNDATIONS, SRC-UCG156, SRC-PLICA, SRC-GRAMMATONOMIA.

## Title VI — Grammar-as-letter promotion and constructive towers

### PIA-061 · VI.01 — Promotion object

**Mandate.** Promote a grammar or certified compositional path to a higher-level letter carrying immutable source identity, external type, interpretation, expansion map, evidence, cost and loss. The letter represents a structured object; it is not merely a new name pasted onto unverified behavior.

**Acceptance.** A promoted grammar can be addressed, inspected, expanded and used in another validated grammar while retaining its original source and contracts.

**Continuity:** K-GEN · K-SEM · K-SRC · K-REPLAY. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-PLICA, SRC-UCG156, SRC-RELATIONAL, SRC-GRAMMATONOMIA.

### PIA-062 · VI.02 — Representation recovery

**Mandate.** Specify what expansion recovers: exact source bytes, canonical serialization, derivation tree or equivalence class. Retaining a pointer is insufficient unless the bytes remain retrievable. Preserve token boundaries and versioned encodings.

**Acceptance.** Delete a working copy and recover the captured source from the package/store; compare the promised bytes or canonical representation exactly.

**Continuity:** K-GEN · K-SEM · K-SRC · K-REPLAY. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-PLICA, SRC-UCG156, SRC-RELATIONAL, SRC-GRAMMATONOMIA.

### PIA-063 · VI.03 — Semantic preservation

**Mandate.** Supply a separate preservation obligation for promoted objects under stated denotation or observations. Lossless syntactic expansion does not imply semantic equivalence across every context. Finite exhaustive checks and formal proofs have different scopes and labels.

**Acceptance.** A finite promotion checks every member of its declared finite language; a broader promotion records its proof or remains proposed with an explicit unproved obligation.

**Continuity:** K-GEN · K-SEM · K-SRC · K-REPLAY. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-PLICA, SRC-UCG156, SRC-RELATIONAL, SRC-GRAMMATONOMIA.

### PIA-064 · VI.04 — Lossy folds and quotients

**Mandate.** A many-to-one promotion declares discarded distinctions, quotient relation and questions no longer answerable. Keep side information when exact recovery is required. Never describe a lossy quotient as globally reversible merely because one representative is stored.

**Acceptance.** A noninjective counterexample demonstrates ambiguity, and a side-data round trip recovers the original where the contract promises it.

**Continuity:** K-GEN · K-SEM · K-SRC · K-REPLAY. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-PLICA, SRC-UCG156, SRC-RELATIONAL, SRC-GRAMMATONOMIA.

### PIA-065 · VI.05 — Explicate, implicate and complicate

**Mandate.** Preserve Plicastratum's named operations and source-specific meanings. Implement expansion/analysis, folding/encapsulation and composed unfolding as versioned operators with domains, invariants and failure states. Avoid substituting intuitive prose for executable laws.

**Acceptance.** At least one source-grounded operator per named operation has fixtures, a negative case and a relation to the original definition.

**Continuity:** K-GEN · K-SEM · K-SRC · K-REPLAY. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-PLICA, SRC-UCG156, SRC-RELATIONAL, SRC-GRAMMATONOMIA.

### PIA-066 · VI.06 — Promotion tower and identity depth

**Mandate.** Represent successive alphabets and their maps as a typed tower. Track identity at representation, state, declared holonomy and chain levels where defined. Seven strata, seven-complete terminology and University division numbers are separate namespaces.

**Acceptance.** A multi-level tower expands to its base representation, reports each preserved/lost property and resolves overloaded terminology without numerical conflation.

**Continuity:** K-GEN · K-SEM · K-SRC · K-REPLAY. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-PLICA, SRC-UCG156, SRC-RELATIONAL, SRC-GRAMMATONOMIA.

### PIA-067 · VI.07 — Trace mining

**Mandate.** Mine repeated admitted trace segments as candidate higher operators. Preserve ordering, parameterization, preconditions, effects and costs. Frequency suggests reuse; it does not prove semantic equivalence or correctness.

**Acceptance.** Mine a repeated trace, propose a macro, verify it against its expansion on declared cases and retain a counterexample for an invalid macro.

**Continuity:** K-GEN · K-SEM · K-SRC · K-REPLAY. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-PLICA, SRC-UCG156, SRC-RELATIONAL, SRC-GRAMMATONOMIA.

### PIA-068 · VI.08 — Structural canonicalization

**Mandate.** Declare normalization rules, symmetry actions and representative selection. Check confluence/termination where claimed, or expose order dependence and finite bounds. Stable content IDs use domain-separated canonical encodings.

**Acceptance.** Isomorphic representations canonicalize under the promised action, nonisomorphic controls remain distinct, and normalization claims are scoped to tested/proved domains.

**Continuity:** K-GEN · K-SEM · K-SRC · K-REPLAY. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-PLICA, SRC-UCG156, SRC-RELATIONAL, SRC-GRAMMATONOMIA.

### PIA-069 · VI.09 — Operator alphabets

**Mandate.** Treat operations, data structures, algorithms, types and complexity descriptors as typed alphabet citizens. A grammar over them specifies valid compositions, policies and cost constraints. Keep implementation choices separate from mathematical denotations.

**Acceptance.** Construct a valid algorithm/data-structure composition and reject an incompatible one, with resulting cost model and witness obligations.

**Continuity:** K-GEN · K-SEM · K-SRC · K-REPLAY. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-PLICA, SRC-UCG156, SRC-RELATIONAL, SRC-GRAMMATONOMIA.

### PIA-070 · VI.10 — Alphabets of grammars

**Mandate.** Support higher grammars whose letters are complete lower grammars with independent namespaces and contracts. Composition declares how lower-language variables, symbols and interpretations align. Resolve collisions explicitly and allow multi-input grammar constructors.

**Acceptance.** Compose two independently versioned grammars into a higher language; inspect both expansions, reject a namespace/type collision and explain the resulting interpretation.

**Continuity:** K-GEN · K-SEM · K-SRC · K-REPLAY. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-PLICA, SRC-UCG156, SRC-RELATIONAL, SRC-GRAMMATONOMIA.

### PIA-071 · VI.11 — Promotion admission and invalidation

**Mandate.** A candidate promotion becomes reusable only after its declared verification and packaging gates. Changed dependency semantics require a new promotion version and dependent revalidation. Old expansions and receipts remain available.

**Acceptance.** Replace one dependency and show impacted promotions lose current eligibility while historical certified versions still resolve.

**Continuity:** K-GEN · K-SEM · K-SRC · K-REPLAY. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-PLICA, SRC-UCG156, SRC-RELATIONAL, SRC-GRAMMATONOMIA.

### PIA-072 · VI.12 — Tower discovery agenda

**Mandate.** Treat new grammar-letter structures as research hypotheses with measurable utility: compression, reuse, interpretation preservation, search cost and explanatory power. Enumerate bounded candidates and counterexamples instead of promising unlimited automatic discovery.

**Acceptance.** A reproducible experiment compares promoted and unpromoted representations, including overhead, losses, failure cases and an explicit continuation frontier.

**Continuity:** K-GEN · K-SEM · K-SRC · K-REPLAY. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-PLICA, SRC-UCG156, SRC-RELATIONAL, SRC-GRAMMATONOMIA.

## Title VII — Q-Strings, typed Q-paths and joint composition

### PIA-073 · VII.01 — Q-String identity

**Mandate.** Preserve the source Q-String record as a classical typed computational relation carrying provenance, context, grammar, evidence and version. Quantum is a house metaphor unless a separate physical model supplies actual quantum states and operations. A verified-looking status string grants no execution authority.

**Acceptance.** Schema/admission tests reject relations missing type/context/evidence and distinguish descriptive records from executable admitted operators.

**Continuity:** K-PATH · K-SEM · K-EVD · K-COST. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-QSTRINGS, SRC-INFINITY, SRC-RELATIONAL, SRC-DK0.

### PIA-074 · VII.02 — Relation before uniqueness

**Mandate.** Represent one-to-many and many-to-many relations before imposing a function. Preserve competing outputs and source disagreements; uniqueness is a separately witnessed property on a declared domain.

**Acceptance.** Reverse lookup returns a candidate set with sources, and an attempted unjustified functional coercion is refused.

**Continuity:** K-PATH · K-SEM · K-EVD · K-COST. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-QSTRINGS, SRC-INFINITY, SRC-RELATIONAL, SRC-DK0.

### PIA-075 · VII.03 — Typed directed hypergraph

**Mandate.** Use named/ordered input and output ports with incidence, types, constraints, context, provenance and time/version. An n-ary operation is one joint hyperedge, not independent unary arcs. Maintain DK0 and EFC source meanings through adapters.

**Acceptance.** A two-input rule cannot fire when only one premise is reachable; swapped noncommutative ports and incorrect multiplicity are detected.

**Continuity:** K-PATH · K-SEM · K-EVD · K-COST. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-QSTRINGS, SRC-INFINITY, SRC-RELATIONAL, SRC-DK0.

### PIA-076 · VII.04 — Q-path composition

**Mandate.** A Q-path composes admissible hyperedges with explicit bindings, context transport, invariant/loss composition and witness aggregation. Record all premises and outputs. Composition legality and the truth of external claims remain separate checks.

**Acceptance.** Execute a multi-step, multi-input path and reconstruct each port binding; reject missing, wrong-type or wrong-context prerequisites.

**Continuity:** K-PATH · K-SEM · K-EVD · K-COST. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-QSTRINGS, SRC-INFINITY, SRC-RELATIONAL, SRC-DK0.

### PIA-077 · VII.05 — Reachability semantics

**Mandate.** Define reachable relative to registered operators, available premises, context, authority and finite resource policy. Fully reachable means addressable/searchable under supported contracts, not that every node has a valid edge to every other node or that every problem is decidable.

**Acceptance.** Search returns found, disproved-under-complete-finite-search, unknown, blocked and resource-limit with reasons and the exact explored boundary.

**Continuity:** K-PATH · K-SEM · K-EVD · K-COST. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-QSTRINGS, SRC-INFINITY, SRC-RELATIONAL, SRC-DK0.

### PIA-078 · VII.06 — Context and witness transport

**Mandate.** A relation preserves only the invariants it declares. Compose source witnesses and expose missing obligations rather than reusing evidence from incompatible contexts. Changes in policy, algebra or units can invalidate a path even when identifiers look similar.

**Acceptance.** A context change triggers revalidation; a compatible transport has a preservation receipt, while missing transports remain unsupported.

**Continuity:** K-PATH · K-SEM · K-EVD · K-COST. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-QSTRINGS, SRC-INFINITY, SRC-RELATIONAL, SRC-DK0.

### PIA-079 · VII.07 — Multicategorical composition

**Mandate.** Treat multiple-input operators and their substitution as typed multimorphisms where the laws actually hold. Declare associativity, identities, symmetry and effects. Noncommutative or effectful composition retains ordering and cannot inherit symmetric laws automatically.

**Acceptance.** Compare two legal bracketings under stated assumptions, and demonstrate a counterexample to swapping effectful or ordered inputs.

**Continuity:** K-PATH · K-SEM · K-EVD · K-COST. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-QSTRINGS, SRC-INFINITY, SRC-RELATIONAL, SRC-DK0.

### PIA-080 · VII.08 — Costs and path planning

**Mandate.** Plan under typed admissibility and explicit cost vectors before heuristic ranking. Keep latency, memory, evidence strength, information loss and effect budgets distinct. A cheaper path is not necessarily more correct or more source-faithful.

**Acceptance.** Competing admissible paths produce a justified Pareto/selected result under a versioned policy, and an invalid low-cost path is rejected.

**Continuity:** K-PATH · K-SEM · K-EVD · K-COST. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-QSTRINGS, SRC-INFINITY, SRC-RELATIONAL, SRC-DK0.

### PIA-081 · VII.09 — Relation kinds and negative edges

**Mandate.** Distinguish implication, analogy, structural isomorphism, representation transport, empirical association, translation, borrowing, causality and policy refusal. A named edge never silently changes kind during composition.

**Acceptance.** Cross-domain examples show which edge kinds compose and which do not; unsupported causal or semantic conclusions are blocked.

**Continuity:** K-PATH · K-SEM · K-EVD · K-COST. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-QSTRINGS, SRC-INFINITY, SRC-RELATIONAL, SRC-DK0.

### PIA-082 · VII.10 — Higher structures with hypotheses

**Mandate.** Distinguish graph cycles, algebraic rings, simplicial nerves, fundamental groups, sheaves and holonomy. Construct them only from the required data and hypotheses; a visual loop is not evidence of every corresponding structure.

**Acceptance.** Nerve/sheaf examples provide intersections or restriction maps and compatibility checks; insufficient input yields a specific missing-hypothesis result.

**Continuity:** K-PATH · K-SEM · K-EVD · K-COST. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-QSTRINGS, SRC-INFINITY, SRC-RELATIONAL, SRC-DK0.

### PIA-083 · VII.11 — Q-path packages and replay

**Mandate.** Package a path with signatures, dependency versions, contexts, source witnesses, cost policy, trace and revalidation procedure. Provide a pure inspection projection and a separately admitted execution interface.

**Acceptance.** Export/import a path, replay its recorded result and execute a new reproduction; historical and current runs have distinct identities.

**Continuity:** K-PATH · K-SEM · K-EVD · K-COST. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-QSTRINGS, SRC-INFINITY, SRC-RELATIONAL, SRC-DK0.

### PIA-084 · VII.12 — Relational opportunity discovery

**Mandate.** Identify absent adapters, inconsistent relations, reusable subpaths and cross-domain candidate laws as research opportunities. Each proposal names its baseline, unsupported step, falsifiable test and expected benefit.

**Acceptance.** The system emits an opportunity from a bounded graph gap with linked evidence and a runnable experiment proposal, without presenting the proposed relation as established.

**Continuity:** K-PATH · K-SEM · K-EVD · K-COST. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-QSTRINGS, SRC-INFINITY, SRC-RELATIONAL, SRC-DK0.

## Title VIII — Native compilation, software units and tool contracts

### PIA-085 · VIII.01 — Native source language

**Mandate.** Deliver a documented native language with lexer, parser, typed AST and intermediate representation. Preserve the original PolyIA native-language obligation. JSON serves APIs, registries and evidence; the bootstrap command envelope is not claimed to replace a scientific native grammar.

**Acceptance.** Parse and compile meaningful source programs, show type errors at source spans, and compare generated execution with an independently checked expected result.

**Continuity:** K-GEN · K-SEM · K-AUTH · K-COST. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-POLYIA96, SRC-UCG156, SRC-ASTRA.

### PIA-086 · VIII.02 — Intermediate representation

**Mandate.** Define PIR and subject IRs with explicit types, contexts, assumptions, dependencies, effects, costs, source spans and proof obligations. Lowering preserves stated semantics or records loss. Do not equate a textual plan with executable code.

**Acceptance.** Round-trip IR serialization and verify at least one linguistic and one nonlinguistic lowering through the same core contract.

**Continuity:** K-GEN · K-SEM · K-AUTH · K-COST. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-POLYIA96, SRC-UCG156, SRC-ASTRA.

### PIA-087 · VIII.03 — Independent computational atoms

**Mandate.** Each atom declares public ports, state lifecycle, version, external semantics, witnesses and budgets. It is independently buildable, testable, replaceable and observable. Size does not determine independence; enforce no undeclared implementation coupling.

**Acceptance.** Install an atom in isolation and substitute a compatible implementation without importing its private internals or silently changing behavior.

**Continuity:** K-GEN · K-SEM · K-AUTH · K-COST. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-POLYIA96, SRC-UCG156, SRC-ASTRA.

### PIA-088 · VIII.04 — Typed module resolution

**Mandate.** Resolve providers by type, version, capabilities and constraints. Enumerate ambiguity rather than silently selecting a similarly named library. ABI incompatibility and missing grants are compilation failures with actionable diagnostics.

**Acceptance.** Positive and negative provider-resolution fixtures cover multiple providers, wrong versions, unavailable tools and incompatible ABI.

**Continuity:** K-GEN · K-SEM · K-AUTH · K-COST. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-POLYIA96, SRC-UCG156, SRC-ASTRA.

### PIA-089 · VIII.05 — SDK and package construction

**Mandate.** Generate specialized SDKs and software packages from admitted compositions through partial evaluation and explicit dependency closure. Avoid bundling every project merely to claim reuse. Keep classes, objects, protocols and language bindings as separate realizations of a common contract.

**Acceptance.** A generated package executes from a clean environment with only declared dependencies and includes its source/evidence manifest.

**Continuity:** K-GEN · K-SEM · K-AUTH · K-COST. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-POLYIA96, SRC-UCG156, SRC-ASTRA.

### PIA-090 · VIII.06 — Tool contract schema

**Mandate.** Every tool declares input/output schemas, preconditions, effect class, data reads, authority scope, limits, timeout, idempotency behavior, cancellation and result/evidence schema. Curl-like network access is an explicit tool, not ambient power granted to all generators.

**Acceptance.** A contract validator and broker reject invalid input, ungranted effects and oversized outputs; successful calls retain actual tool version and receipts.

**Continuity:** K-GEN · K-SEM · K-AUTH · K-COST. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-POLYIA96, SRC-UCG156, SRC-ASTRA.

### PIA-091 · VIII.07 — Tool broker and isolation

**Mandate.** Invoke tools only through an admitted broker. Pure kernels, local storage, network readers, mutators and unsafe native plugins have different capability profiles. Use OS/process isolation where required and minimize ephemeral memory scopes without claiming that scoped variables form a sandbox.

**Acceptance.** Denied filesystem/network/process operations fail in an isolation test; the broker records dispatch, timeout/cancellation and output custody.

**Continuity:** K-GEN · K-SEM · K-AUTH · K-COST. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-POLYIA96, SRC-UCG156, SRC-ASTRA.

### PIA-092 · VIII.08 — Generator and witness roles

**Mandate.** Declare constructor, normalizer, filter, oracle/witness and renderer roles separately. Native generation cannot secretly read sealed witness answers. A library used during construction must be declared as part of construction and cannot be presented as an independent post-seal witness for the same claim.

**Acceptance.** Role/import/read audits detect witness leakage and the inherited RDKit-role mismatch; revised experiments identify dependencies and independent checks honestly.

**Continuity:** K-GEN · K-SEM · K-AUTH · K-COST. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-POLYIA96, SRC-UCG156, SRC-ASTRA.

### PIA-093 · VIII.09 — Execution admission

**Mandate.** Generated code, plans, grammar paths and model proposals remain untrusted candidate artifacts until type, effect, resource and verification gates admit them. A corpus executable flag or hash alone cannot authorize running it.

**Acceptance.** Attempts to run unregistered handlers, eval strings or source-embedded commands are rejected; admitted code resolves to a specific verified package version.

**Continuity:** K-GEN · K-SEM · K-AUTH · K-COST. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-POLYIA96, SRC-UCG156, SRC-ASTRA.

### PIA-094 · VIII.10 — Language-neutral interfaces

**Mandate.** Use stable schemas and IDL/WIT where supported. Provide real tested Python and JavaScript/TypeScript adapters first, then native/WASM bindings when tooling is present. Record unsupported hosts rather than shipping fabricated successful stubs.

**Acceptance.** Cross-language contract tests exercise the same state command and scientific operation, including refusal behavior and version mismatch.

**Continuity:** K-GEN · K-SEM · K-AUTH · K-COST. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-POLYIA96, SRC-UCG156, SRC-ASTRA.

### PIA-095 · VIII.11 — Model tool use as a client contract

**Mandate.** Examine Hermes, OpenCode and the intended OpenCLAR/OpenClaw reference using official current sources. Extract their tool-call schema/broker ideas where useful. Keep language models, coding agents and orchestration tools distinct; unresolved product identity remains explicit.

**Acceptance.** An architecture comparison cites exact versions and maps transferable mechanisms to PolyIA contracts; the required no-LLM path passes with every optional model adapter disabled.

**Continuity:** K-GEN · K-SEM · K-AUTH · K-COST. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-POLYIA96, SRC-UCG156, SRC-ASTRA.

### PIA-096 · VIII.12 — Effects, memory and protocols

**Mandate.** Model filesystem, database, network and persistent-state effects explicitly in software/state-machine contracts. Ephemeral workspaces have scoped lifetimes and cleanup receipts. Protocol evolutions preserve command compatibility or require negotiated versions and migrations.

**Acceptance.** Tests cover resource cleanup, incompatible protocol versions, cancellation and external-effect uncertainty without losing the associated evidence.

**Continuity:** K-GEN · K-SEM · K-AUTH · K-COST. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-POLYIA96, SRC-UCG156, SRC-ASTRA.

## Title IX — Constructive generation and state-map models

### PIA-097 · IX.01 — Constructive generation

**Mandate.** A generator produces objects from declared primitives and rules, with derivation traces and bounded search. Distinguish generation, recognition, retrieval, interpolation and unconstrained proposal. A retrieved example is not evidence that a generative law produced it.

**Acceptance.** Generate a previously unlisted admissible object under a finite contract and retain a replayable derivation plus an independent checker result.

**Continuity:** K-GEN · K-STATE · K-EVD · K-COST. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCG156, SRC-POLYIA96, SRC-TRE, SRC-RELATIONAL.

### PIA-098 · IX.02 — Generative model contract

**Mandate.** Define each model by input/output types, parameters/state, generation law, constraints, declared reads, randomness, evidence and costs. A model need not be an LLM or a neural network. Store learned parameters separately from grammar rules and runtime policy.

**Acceptance.** Model schema validates grammar-based, probabilistic and optional neural instances with distinct capabilities and no hidden inference dependency.

**Continuity:** K-GEN · K-STATE · K-EVD · K-COST. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCG156, SRC-POLYIA96, SRC-TRE, SRC-RELATIONAL.

### PIA-099 · IX.03 — Non-LLM language generation

**Mandate.** Implement a useful bounded example using finite-state transduction, typed templates, morphology and/or a probabilistic grammar. Generate terminology-aware explanations with source references and explicit supported intent coverage. Do not promise arbitrary open-domain comprehension from the existence of a state machine.

**Acceptance.** Produce different valid tones/representations from one verified content plan, preserve every factual relation and reject unsupported requested claims.

**Continuity:** K-GEN · K-STATE · K-EVD · K-COST. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCG156, SRC-POLYIA96, SRC-TRE, SRC-RELATIONAL.

### PIA-100 · IX.04 — State-map accompaniment

**Mandate.** Package generative models with a state-map controller that tracks accepted input, candidate generation, constraints, verification, representation choices, tool calls and refusal. The map provides inspectable search and workflow structure; it is not infinite memory or unlimited semantic understanding.

**Acceptance.** Inspect and replay a model's state trace, change an admitted style choice and observe output variation without changing certified content.

**Continuity:** K-GEN · K-STATE · K-EVD · K-COST. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCG156, SRC-POLYIA96, SRC-TRE, SRC-RELATIONAL.

### PIA-101 · IX.05 — Optional narrow neural models

**Mandate.** Permit pretrained non-LLM speech, acoustic, ranking, recognition or other narrow models only as declared optional components with version, license, inputs, measured behavior and resource costs. Determine whether a chosen component contains an LLM rather than assuming its product label.

**Acceptance.** Compare a narrow model with the deterministic baseline, including errors and latency; disabling it preserves every core acceptance workflow.

**Continuity:** K-GEN · K-STATE · K-EVD · K-COST. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCG156, SRC-POLYIA96, SRC-TRE, SRC-RELATIONAL.

### PIA-102 · IX.06 — Constraint-driven model construction

**Mandate.** Compile a problem's typed grammar, state map, available tools and verified operations into a specialized generator. Program specialization may be fast without retraining weights. A new model package needs its own boundaries, acceptance and identity.

**Acceptance.** Given a supported commission, emit an independently executable model/package with source lock, constraints and tests, then run it in a clean environment.

**Continuity:** K-GEN · K-STATE · K-EVD · K-COST. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCG156, SRC-POLYIA96, SRC-TRE, SRC-RELATIONAL.

### PIA-103 · IX.07 — Randomness and reproducibility

**Mandate.** Declare deterministic and stochastic components. Record seed, algorithm, distribution, dependency version and sampling budget. Reproducibility of a sampled run is distinct from statistical validity or exhaustive coverage.

**Acceptance.** Reproduce fixed-seed outputs and run a separate distributional evaluation with denominators and uncertainty; no random result is labeled proof merely because it repeats.

**Continuity:** K-GEN · K-STATE · K-EVD · K-COST. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCG156, SRC-POLYIA96, SRC-TRE, SRC-RELATIONAL.

### PIA-104 · IX.08 — Inverse and relational generation

**Mandate.** Generate preimages or candidate explanations as a relation with domain, search policy, uniqueness status and witness obligations. Separate no preimage under a proved finite domain from not found under a budget.

**Acceptance.** Inverse fixtures include unique, multiple, impossible-in-declared-domain and unresolved cases with source and counterexample records.

**Continuity:** K-GEN · K-STATE · K-EVD · K-COST. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCG156, SRC-POLYIA96, SRC-TRE, SRC-RELATIONAL.

### PIA-105 · IX.09 — Curriculum and explanation generation

**Mandate.** Generate learning sequences from formal prerequisites, source coverage and tested examples. Explanations retain assumptions, notation translations and evidence grades. The user can move from elementary fractions through polynomial division to derivative rules without losing the distinctions between them.

**Acceptance.** A curriculum path identifies prerequisites and derives the polynomial/product/quotient connection using actual calculations and inspectable source-linked steps.

**Continuity:** K-GEN · K-STATE · K-EVD · K-COST. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCG156, SRC-POLYIA96, SRC-TRE, SRC-RELATIONAL.

### PIA-106 · IX.10 — Machine and package synthesis

**Mandate.** Synthesize state machines, APIs, protocols, classes or SDKs only within registered constructive families. Every production carries an executable behavior contract, interface dependencies and verification plan. General program synthesis remains a research frontier with decidability and cost limits.

**Acceptance.** Synthesize two distinct runnable packages under bounded grammar families, check their contracts and retain a failed synthesis with a precise unsupported/budget result.

**Continuity:** K-GEN · K-STATE · K-EVD · K-COST. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCG156, SRC-POLYIA96, SRC-TRE, SRC-RELATIONAL.

### PIA-107 · IX.11 — Optimization without semantic drift

**Mandate.** Search for transformations that improve declared metrics while preserving required observations, effects and source custody. Keep baseline and candidate results separate. A syntactically shorter or faster output may violate other constraints.

**Acceptance.** An optimization experiment includes semantic regression, adverse cases, total production cost and a measured improvement threshold before admission.

**Continuity:** K-GEN · K-STATE · K-EVD · K-COST. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCG156, SRC-POLYIA96, SRC-TRE, SRC-RELATIONAL.

### PIA-108 · IX.12 — Generative frontier governance

**Mandate.** Continuously enumerate supported experiment opportunities under budgets and standing authority. Track explored regions, equivalent candidates, promising gaps and counterexamples. Do not equate a running loop with productive discovery.

**Acceptance.** The worker records generated, duplicate, refused, tested and admitted counts, plus resource use and meaningful stop/pause conditions.

**Continuity:** K-GEN · K-STATE · K-EVD · K-COST. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCG156, SRC-POLYIA96, SRC-TRE, SRC-RELATIONAL.

## Title X — Mathematics, science and computer-science coverage

### PIA-109 · X.01 — Mathematics coverage atlas

**Mandate.** Register canonical University subjects and conventional mathematical fields, using versioned external taxonomies as navigation aids. Include logic, sets, algebra, analysis, geometry, topology, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, number theory and applied mathematics. Taxonomic inclusion does not assert implementation.

**Acceptance.** A complete topic inventory preserves existing IDs and maps every inherited mathematics obligation to its capability/evidence state and further dependencies.

**Continuity:** K-COVER · K-SEM · K-EVD · K-GEN. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCG156, SRC-UCGFOUNDATIONS, REPO-GRAMMARINNUMBERS, REPO-COMPUTATIONALGRAMMARTHEORY.

### PIA-110 · X.02 — Computer science coverage atlas

**Mandate.** Include computability, languages, automata, algorithms, complexity, data structures, programming languages, type systems, compilers, databases, distributed systems, software design and learning methods. Model their structural and operational relations rather than grouping by names alone.

**Acceptance.** Each inherited CS topic has source-linked operators or an explicit research gap; compare at least one algorithm/data-structure/cost combination through a typed path.

**Continuity:** K-COVER · K-SEM · K-EVD · K-GEN. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCG156, SRC-UCGFOUNDATIONS, REPO-GRAMMARINNUMBERS, REPO-COMPUTATIONALGRAMMARTHEORY.

### PIA-111 · X.03 — Exact arithmetic and polynomial forms

**Mandate.** Implement integer/rational arithmetic, field-scoped polynomial division, factorization under declared supported algorithms and rational-function domain guards. Distinguish Euclidean quotient/remainder from fractional division and derivative quotient rules while deriving their legitimate connection.

**Acceptance.** For supplied a,b in K[x], certify a=bq+r and the remainder bound; compare product-rule and quotient-rule derivatives on b(x) nonzero and retain cancellation exclusions.

**Continuity:** K-COVER · K-SEM · K-EVD · K-GEN. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCG156, SRC-UCGFOUNDATIONS, REPO-GRAMMARINNUMBERS, REPO-COMPUTATIONALGRAMMARTHEORY.

### PIA-112 · X.04 — Calculus and integration methods

**Mandate.** Preserve term grammars, differentiation, higher-derivative orbit analysis, Leibniz/Faa di Bruno patterns, limits, series, integration-method machines and the Liouville/nonelementarity boundary. A failed integration search is not a proof of no elementary antiderivative.

**Acceptance.** Each supported method has domain-aware positive/negative cases and a derivative witness; unsupported elementary/non-elementary classification remains explicit.

**Continuity:** K-COVER · K-SEM · K-EVD · K-GEN. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCG156, SRC-UCGFOUNDATIONS, REPO-GRAMMARINNUMBERS, REPO-COMPUTATIONALGRAMMARTHEORY.

### PIA-113 · X.05 — Linear algebra and algebraic structures

**Mandate.** Support typed matrices, composition, systems, decompositions, linear maps, groups, rings and fields under stated domains. Separate a matrix display from the computation it denotes. Preserve construction gaps and distinguish split extensions from non-split ones accurately.

**Acceptance.** Dimension/type checks, exact residuals and structure laws validate examples; the inherited A4/non-split claim is corrected with the original preserved.

**Continuity:** K-COVER · K-SEM · K-EVD · K-GEN. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCG156, SRC-UCGFOUNDATIONS, REPO-GRAMMARINNUMBERS, REPO-COMPUTATIONALGRAMMARTHEORY.

### PIA-114 · X.06 — Topology and relational structure

**Mandate.** Preserve simplicial complexes, finite homology, Euler characteristic, scoped fundamental group presentations and topologies of forms/worlds. State coefficient fields and what invariants can or cannot classify. Do not infer integral torsion or complete homeomorphism classification from rational/F2 ranks.

**Acceptance.** Boundary-squared tests and independently checked examples identify coefficient choices, limitations and relevant source amendments.

**Continuity:** K-COVER · K-SEM · K-EVD · K-GEN. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCG156, SRC-UCGFOUNDATIONS, REPO-GRAMMARINNUMBERS, REPO-COMPUTATIONALGRAMMARTHEORY.

### PIA-115 · X.07 — Numerical mathematics

**Mandate.** Treat ODE solvers, Runge–Kutta/Butcher trees, phase portraits, numerical integration, error and stability as machines with method-specific assumptions and tolerances. Separate rounding, discretization, sampling and model errors.

**Acceptance.** A reproducible solver comparison includes convergence/error checks, stability limits, step policy, failures and actual cost measurements.

**Continuity:** K-COVER · K-SEM · K-EVD · K-GEN. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCG156, SRC-UCGFOUNDATIONS, REPO-GRAMMARINNUMBERS, REPO-COMPUTATIONALGRAMMARTHEORY.

### PIA-116 · X.08 — Chemistry alphabet and grammar

**Mandate.** Preserve UCG's element, orbital, valence, compound, molecule, nomenclature, symmetry, stereochemistry and stoichiometry obligations as scientific computational models. Distinguish notation, graph admissibility, empirical stability and physical synthesis. Element ordering rules and exceptions require separate evidence.

**Acceptance.** Reproduce scoped element/molecule experiments with declared generator/witness roles, symmetry counts, negative controls and source-linked exceptions.

**Continuity:** K-COVER · K-SEM · K-EVD · K-GEN. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCG156, SRC-UCGFOUNDATIONS, REPO-GRAMMARINNUMBERS, REPO-COMPUTATIONALGRAMMARTHEORY.

### PIA-117 · X.09 — Forms, structures and scientific models

**Mandate.** Preserve graph/tree/ring enumeration, resonance and aromaticity models, substituents, reaction/biochemical grammar proposals and optional energy denotations under their source scopes. House calculus of forms is a defined research program, not an automatic replacement for physical law.

**Acceptance.** Each supported form grammar declares domain, invariants and witness set; wrong-witness audits and model-specific exclusions remain inspectable.

**Continuity:** K-COVER · K-SEM · K-EVD · K-GEN. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCG156, SRC-UCGFOUNDATIONS, REPO-GRAMMARINNUMBERS, REPO-COMPUTATIONALGRAMMARTHEORY.

### PIA-118 · X.10 — Units, measurement and reality

**Mandate.** Carry dimensional analysis, measurement uncertainty, dataset selection and calibration through empirical computations. Keep simulation, visualization, theoretical derivation and observation distinct. A grammar's realizable word is not automatically an experimentally stable object.

**Acceptance.** Cross-domain tests reject dimensionally invalid operations, distinguish measured/simulated data and retain calibration/source metadata.

**Continuity:** K-COVER · K-SEM · K-EVD · K-GEN. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCG156, SRC-UCGFOUNDATIONS, REPO-GRAMMARINNUMBERS, REPO-COMPUTATIONALGRAMMARTHEORY.

### PIA-119 · X.11 — Domain registry and subject machines

**Mandate.** Give each subject a consistent contract for alphabet, grammar, in-grammar, denotation, operators, costs, witnesses and machines, while preserving its real mathematical differences. Add subject-specific acceptance adapters rather than forcing every field into a single solver.

**Acceptance.** The registry covers all inherited subject obligations, executes representative machines and marks unsupported operations without fabricated placeholders.

**Continuity:** K-COVER · K-SEM · K-EVD · K-GEN. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCG156, SRC-UCGFOUNDATIONS, REPO-GRAMMARINNUMBERS, REPO-COMPUTATIONALGRAMMARTHEORY.

### PIA-120 · X.12 — Open scientific obligations

**Mandate.** Track unsolved translations, proofs, algorithms, models and missing independent witnesses as first-class research obligations. Each names prerequisites, attempted methods, negative results, cost bounds and what would count as progress.

**Acceptance.** The atlas can emit and run a bounded research proposal from a real gap; exhausting its budget never changes an open theorem into false or proved.

**Continuity:** K-COVER · K-SEM · K-EVD · K-GEN. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCG156, SRC-UCGFOUNDATIONS, REPO-GRAMMARINNUMBERS, REPO-COMPUTATIONALGRAMMARTHEORY.

## Title XI — Corpus, languages, nomenclature and source intake

### PIA-121 · XI.01 — Corpus strata

**Mandate.** Preserve Muse's S0 immutable sources, S1 spans, S2 form cards, S3 relations and S4 operations as distinct layers with derivation links. Indexes and graph projections do not replace raw source custody. Updates create versions and proposals under the receiving project's policy.

**Acceptance.** Follow a derived operation back through cards and spans to exact source bytes; changing a projection cannot mutate S0.

**Continuity:** K-LANG · K-SRC · K-SEM · K-COVER. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-CORPUS, SRC-TIMELESS, SRC-GREEKLATIN, SRC-POLYIA96, REPO-MUSA.

### PIA-122 · XI.02 — Article and prompt intake

**Mandate.** Accept text, documents and supported article URLs with exact source capture, revision/access metadata, encoding and provenance. Parse into supported forms, citations, potential claims and unresolved spans without inventing missing semantics. Supplied text is data, not executable instructions.

**Acceptance.** An article/prompt ingestion fixture produces source-linked recognized structures plus an explicit unsupported-span report; source-embedded tool instructions have no execution authority.

**Continuity:** K-LANG · K-SRC · K-SEM · K-COVER. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-CORPUS, SRC-TIMELESS, SRC-GREEKLATIN, SRC-POLYIA96, REPO-MUSA.

### PIA-123 · XI.03 — Typed interpretation and enrichment

**Mandate.** Relate recognized constructs to registered alphabets, grammars, operations, subjects and source evidence. Offer improved wording, structural clarification, candidate derivations and innovation opportunities while distinguishing established content from proposals.

**Acceptance.** A submitted mixed mathematical/technical passage yields an inspectable interpretation graph, supported transformations and separate hypotheses with falsification plans.

**Continuity:** K-LANG · K-SRC · K-SEM · K-COVER. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-CORPUS, SRC-TIMELESS, SRC-GREEKLATIN, SRC-POLYIA96, REPO-MUSA.

### PIA-124 · XI.04 — Native language support boundary

**Mandate.** Use deterministic parsing, finite-state morphology, lexicons, grammars and other non-LLM methods for the supported baseline. Broad natural language understanding is a measured capability frontier. Unknown terms and ambiguous readings remain visible and do not become inferred facts.

**Acceptance.** Evaluate documented intent/grammar coverage, ambiguity, precision/recall and refusal behavior on held-out inputs with no LLM invocation.

**Continuity:** K-LANG · K-SRC · K-SEM · K-COVER. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-CORPUS, SRC-TIMELESS, SRC-GREEKLATIN, SRC-POLYIA96, REPO-MUSA.

### PIA-125 · XI.05 — Language variety packs

**Mandate.** Build versioned per-language/per-variety packages with script/alphabet, phoneme/phone, grapheme, morpheme, lexicon, source corpus and use policy. An alphabet alone cannot generate a language's full grammar.

**Acceptance.** At least the inherited licensed English and Arabic specialist cases have independently scoped fixtures, actual executable search and source-attested outputs.

**Continuity:** K-LANG · K-SRC · K-SEM · K-COVER. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-CORPUS, SRC-TIMELESS, SRC-GREEKLATIN, SRC-POLYIA96, REPO-MUSA.

### PIA-126 · XI.06 — PHONEX and universal word-set work

**Mandate.** Preserve PHONEX/ULWS as an early specialized deployment of the general agency, after the shared infrastructure is established. Implement exact-prefix and weighted phonetic search with declared semiring, symbol alignment, cost and evidence.

**Acceptance.** Cross-language composition and noninitial negative controls execute on attested corpora; comparisons include dictionary/trie/FST/scan baselines and evidence errors.

**Continuity:** K-LANG · K-SRC · K-SEM · K-COVER. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-CORPUS, SRC-TIMELESS, SRC-GREEKLATIN, SRC-POLYIA96, REPO-MUSA.

### PIA-127 · XI.07 — Linguistic relation discipline

**Mandate.** Keep pronunciation similarity, transliteration, translation, cognacy, borrowing, calque, etymology and semantic association as different relation types. Require independent source evidence before historical promotion. Preserve alternatives and varieties.

**Acceptance.** A phonetic match cannot automatically become a cognate/borrowing claim; fixtures include unknown and contradictory source cases.

**Continuity:** K-LANG · K-SRC · K-SEM · K-COVER. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-CORPUS, SRC-TIMELESS, SRC-GREEKLATIN, SRC-POLYIA96, REPO-MUSA.

### PIA-128 · XI.08 — Timeless and rasm bridge

**Mandate.** Preserve original Arabic text and the packet's contextual quotient alphabet and dot/position charts. Inversion returns candidates under the declared table; modern chart equivalence is not a universal historical paleography claim. Keep this bridge outside the existing public SU subject registry.

**Acceptance.** Reproduce the packet's scoped rasm example and candidate count, verify original-text recovery where side data exists, and test contextual distinctions.

**Continuity:** K-LANG · K-SRC · K-SEM · K-COVER. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-CORPUS, SRC-TIMELESS, SRC-GREEKLATIN, SRC-POLYIA96, REPO-MUSA.

### PIA-129 · XI.09 — WAZNOMIA name/function relation

**Mandate.** Preserve name-to-function and function-to-name as partial set-valued relations with witnesses, source scope and loss. Formal nomenclature can be executable under a declared grammar; arbitrary natural-language names do not thereby become trustworthy programs.

**Acceptance.** Both directions produce supported candidates, ambiguity and no-supported-result outcomes; unsupported etymologies are not synthesized as facts.

**Continuity:** K-LANG · K-SRC · K-SEM · K-COVER. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-CORPUS, SRC-TIMELESS, SRC-GREEKLATIN, SRC-POLYIA96, REPO-MUSA.

### PIA-130 · XI.10 — Greek and Latin determinations

**Mandate.** Apply the supplied morphology/nomenclature rules with source custody and a distinction between forms, historical transmission and modern technical convention. Borrowing, calque and unknown are valid outputs. Do not claim a parser exists where the source supplies only a research specification.

**Acceptance.** Implemented parser scope is documented and tested on positive, negative and ambiguous examples; gaps remain explicit scientific obligations.

**Continuity:** K-LANG · K-SRC · K-SEM · K-COVER. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-CORPUS, SRC-TIMELESS, SRC-GREEKLATIN, SRC-POLYIA96, REPO-MUSA.

### PIA-131 · XI.11 — Cross-script and notation transport

**Mandate.** Build reversible or loss-declared transports among scripts, phonetic forms, mathematical notation, machine IR and accessible explanations. Keep exact source spelling alongside normalization. Different transport kinds share infrastructure but retain their own semantic requirements.

**Acceptance.** At least one language transport and one mathematical notation transport preserve stated invariants and expose ambiguity/loss to human and API clients.

**Continuity:** K-LANG · K-SRC · K-SEM · K-COVER. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-CORPUS, SRC-TIMELESS, SRC-GREEKLATIN, SRC-POLYIA96, REPO-MUSA.

### PIA-132 · XI.12 — Corpus growth and privacy

**Mandate.** Ingest new sources with deduplication, rights metadata, span custody and provenance. Separate private content from public exports and preserve authorized access constraints. A new article may propose a grammar relation, but admission waits for tests and evidence.

**Acceptance.** A corpus update creates new versions and opportunities, respects export policy and cannot silently promote a proposed relation to established knowledge.

**Continuity:** K-LANG · K-SRC · K-SEM · K-COVER. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-CORPUS, SRC-TIMELESS, SRC-GREEKLATIN, SRC-POLYIA96, REPO-MUSA.

## Title XII — Experiments, evidence and continuous inquiry

### PIA-133 · XII.01 — Experiment lifecycle

**Mandate.** Use a declared lifecycle including propose, generate, seal, witness, recognize, account, verify and checkpoint as appropriate. Preserve UCG's seal-before-witness principle. Experimental results include failures, unknowns and counterexamples, not only successes.

**Acceptance.** Event history shows generator output sealed before the independent witness is accessed; illegal sequencing is refused.

**Continuity:** K-EVD · K-GEN · K-COST · K-REPLAY. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCG156, SRC-INFINITY, SRC-RECON, SRC-TRE.

### PIA-134 · XII.02 — Enforced read declarations

**Mandate.** A generator's permitted inputs and witness separation must be enforced by the tool/process boundary rather than documentation alone. Include dataset/version identities, filesystem grants and hidden-state controls.

**Acceptance.** A deliberately witness-reading generator is blocked, and the receipt names the denied resource without exposing protected content.

**Continuity:** K-EVD · K-GEN · K-COST · K-REPLAY. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCG156, SRC-INFINITY, SRC-RECON, SRC-TRE.

### PIA-135 · XII.03 — Evidence identity and independence

**Mandate.** A witness records method, assumptions, implementation provenance, inputs, outputs and independence relationship. Recomputing with the same implementation is self-consistency; genuinely independent baselines have separately identified methods or code.

**Acceptance.** Evidence registry distinguishes self-check, differential check, exact finite check and proof; a claimed independent witness sharing the same oracle is flagged.

**Continuity:** K-EVD · K-GEN · K-COST · K-REPLAY. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCG156, SRC-INFINITY, SRC-RECON, SRC-TRE.

### PIA-136 · XII.04 — Exact and symbolic proof scope

**Mandate.** Use exact arithmetic or proof certificates for supported finite/algebraic claims; formal proofs include complete hypotheses and trusted-kernel information. Symbolic simplification carries domains. Numerical agreement cannot discharge a universal symbolic obligation.

**Acceptance.** Known domain/cancellation and vacuous-sampling counterexamples fail the wrong verifier and pass only the appropriate scoped check.

**Continuity:** K-EVD · K-GEN · K-COST · K-REPLAY. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCG156, SRC-INFINITY, SRC-RECON, SRC-TRE.

### PIA-137 · XII.05 — Empirical and statistical evaluation

**Mandate.** Report dataset composition, denominators, sampling, train/held-out separation, precision, recall, error types, uncertainty and negative controls. A witness-derived amendment is labeled witness-informed and assessed on independent held-out cases.

**Acceptance.** An experiment's metrics can be recalculated from retained outputs and witnesses, including its misses and contradictions.

**Continuity:** K-EVD · K-GEN · K-COST · K-REPLAY. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCG156, SRC-INFINITY, SRC-RECON, SRC-TRE.

### PIA-138 · XII.06 — Witness disagreement and audits

**Mandate.** Audit both the generator and witness when they disagree. Version corrected witness models and retain earlier results with their original scope. A benchmark dataset does not define universal possibility.

**Acceptance.** Reproduce a documented wrong-witness case, publish the correction and re-evaluate affected claims without rewriting history.

**Continuity:** K-EVD · K-GEN · K-COST · K-REPLAY. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCG156, SRC-INFINITY, SRC-RECON, SRC-TRE.

### PIA-139 · XII.07 — Continuous worker

**Mandate.** Run a supervised bounded worker on the target VM with queues, leases, checkpoints, budgets, pause/resume and failure backoff. Persist progress across restarts. The package's finite demonstration worker is a seed, not evidence of indefinite production operation.

**Acceptance.** A deployed worker survives restart, obeys pause and quotas, avoids duplicate admission and records measured activity over a declared observation period.

**Continuity:** K-EVD · K-GEN · K-COST · K-REPLAY. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCG156, SRC-INFINITY, SRC-RECON, SRC-TRE.

### PIA-140 · XII.08 — Experiment proposal generation

**Mandate.** Derive candidate experiments from typed graph gaps, grammar deficits, failed inverses, repeated traces and benchmark regressions. Each proposal names baseline, hypothesis, variation space, witness, budget and admission criterion.

**Acceptance.** Generate a proposal from an actual recorded gap and execute its bounded design, preserving both promising and failed outcomes.

**Continuity:** K-EVD · K-GEN · K-COST · K-REPLAY. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCG156, SRC-INFINITY, SRC-RECON, SRC-TRE.

### PIA-141 · XII.09 — Reproduction and regression

**Mandate.** Pin source, code, dependencies, configuration and seeds. Reproduce separately from journal replay, then run regressions for affected capability families. Avoid broad unmotivated testing; target concrete risk and mandatory gates.

**Acceptance.** A clean checkout reproduces selected results and executes scoped negative controls; a changed dependency produces a new run/version comparison.

**Continuity:** K-EVD · K-GEN · K-COST · K-REPLAY. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCG156, SRC-INFINITY, SRC-RECON, SRC-TRE.

### PIA-142 · XII.10 — Cost and performance evidence

**Mandate.** Measure cold/warm latency, quantiles, throughput, build and index cost, memory, storage and total package production cost under documented hardware and sample counts. Include cases where provenance or compilation costs make PolyIA slower.

**Acceptance.** Benchmark reports compare fair baselines with fixed fixtures and explicitly state overhead, uncertainty and unsupported performance claims.

**Continuity:** K-EVD · K-GEN · K-COST · K-REPLAY. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCG156, SRC-INFINITY, SRC-RECON, SRC-TRE.

### PIA-143 · XII.11 — Counterexample and negative-result registry

**Mandate.** Keep immutable counterexamples, failed candidates, exhausted searches and contradictory witnesses with version scope and review response. Negative results improve grammar boundaries without automatic universalization.

**Acceptance.** A prior counterexample remains queryable after a corrected release and prevents re-admitting the same invalid transformation.

**Continuity:** K-EVD · K-GEN · K-COST · K-REPLAY. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCG156, SRC-INFINITY, SRC-RECON, SRC-TRE.

### PIA-144 · XII.12 — Experiment acceptance record

**Mandate.** Completion of an experiment requires produced outputs, sealed inputs, actual witness receipts, verifier results and accounting. Formatting a valid JSON document or SHA-like string is insufficient. A successful experiment's evidence class is displayed everywhere it is reused.

**Acceptance.** Tampered, missing, stale and caller-fabricated receipts fail admission; accepted experiments resolve to actual bytes and scoped scientific claims.

**Continuity:** K-EVD · K-GEN · K-COST · K-REPLAY. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-UCG156, SRC-INFINITY, SRC-RECON, SRC-TRE.

## Title XIII — Versioned improvement, modularity and package evolution

### PIA-145 · XIII.01 — Candidate lifecycle

**Mandate.** Improvements move through proposal, implementation, verification, comparison, admission, activation and monitored operation. Keep research proposals separate from installed capability versions. Continuous learning means controlled capability evolution, not an unsupported claim of magically improving model weights.

**Acceptance.** A candidate progresses only with required evidence, and a rejected candidate cannot become active through a status-field edit.

**Continuity:** K-EVOLVE · K-SHIP · K-EVD · K-REPLAY. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-POLYIA96, SRC-UCG156, SRC-RECON.

### PIA-146 · XIII.02 — Version identity

**Mandate.** Assign immutable versions to grammar, alphabet, operator, model, state schema, compiler, tool contract, dataset and package. Record dependency locks and supersession edges. Human-friendly names resolve through explicit versions or a versioned selection policy.

**Acceptance.** Historical clients resolve the original implementation after a newer version is active; ambiguous unpinned resolution is rejected or explicitly policy-selected.

**Continuity:** K-EVOLVE · K-SHIP · K-EVD · K-REPLAY. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-POLYIA96, SRC-UCG156, SRC-RECON.

### PIA-147 · XIII.03 — Improvement thresholds

**Mandate.** Define baseline, metrics, tolerances, regression obligations and resource policy before evaluation. Improvement may trade speed, accuracy, coverage, interpretability and storage; retain the multidimensional result. Do not automatically supersede a trusted component on one favorable benchmark.

**Acceptance.** A candidate that improves latency but breaks semantics fails admission; a documented tradeoff requires the authorized selection policy.

**Continuity:** K-EVOLVE · K-SHIP · K-EVD · K-REPLAY. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-POLYIA96, SRC-UCG156, SRC-RECON.

### PIA-148 · XIII.04 — Impact analysis

**Mandate.** Trace dependent grammars, Q-paths, SDKs, source claims and state machines affected by a changed contract. Revalidate impacted boundaries and preserve unaffected historical evidence with its original version scope.

**Acceptance.** Modify a low-level atom and show the exact affected dependency closure, required rechecks and still-valid independent packages.

**Continuity:** K-EVOLVE · K-SHIP · K-EVD · K-REPLAY. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-POLYIA96, SRC-UCG156, SRC-RECON.

### PIA-149 · XIII.05 — Activation epoch and rollback

**Mandate.** Activate admitted releases through explicit state transitions binding package digest, policy, compatible state migration and previous epoch. Rollback restores a compatible retained release and accounts for irreversible external effects separately.

**Acceptance.** Rehearse activation and rollback with a fixture, verify version selection and document any state/effect that cannot be undone.

**Continuity:** K-EVOLVE · K-SHIP · K-EVD · K-REPLAY. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-POLYIA96, SRC-UCG156, SRC-RECON.

### PIA-150 · XIII.06 — Modular packaging

**Mandate.** Organize cohesive independently testable packages with declared ownership and public interfaces. Shared infrastructure serves all divisions; VII/VIII research does not monopolize the harness, packaging or verification services. Avoid a miscellaneous shared-utilities dependency sink.

**Acceptance.** Dependency graph and isolated installation tests demonstrate replacement, source custody and absence of undeclared private imports.

**Continuity:** K-EVOLVE · K-SHIP · K-EVD · K-REPLAY. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-POLYIA96, SRC-UCG156, SRC-RECON.

### PIA-151 · XIII.07 — Package manifests and custody

**Mandate.** Every package includes version, sources, licenses, build instructions, dependency lock, types/effects, evidence, limits and migration information. Preserve original authorship and modification history. A content hash identifies bytes but does not imply a license grant or truth.

**Acceptance.** Manifest verification checks actual bytes and dependencies; redistribution/export applies declared rights and policy.

**Continuity:** K-EVOLVE · K-SHIP · K-EVD · K-REPLAY. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-POLYIA96, SRC-UCG156, SRC-RECON.

### PIA-152 · XIII.08 — Compatibility and migration

**Mandate.** Publish schema/API compatibility rules and tested migrations. Database and event schema upgrades keep historical records readable by retained decoders. A new verifier version cannot silently rewrite an old receipt's meaning.

**Acceptance.** Upgrade a stored fixture, verify old event decoding and semantic state, and reject an incompatible client with actionable diagnostics.

**Continuity:** K-EVOLVE · K-SHIP · K-EVD · K-REPLAY. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-POLYIA96, SRC-UCG156, SRC-RECON.

### PIA-153 · XIII.09 — Research branches and release boundaries

**Mandate.** Keep candidate implementation branches, source archives and admitted runtime packages distinct. Isolate experiments from active service state and source repositories. Changes to shared work are reviewed against their contracts before activation.

**Acceptance.** An experiment crash or invalid code candidate cannot mutate the active package or original source snapshot.

**Continuity:** K-EVOLVE · K-SHIP · K-EVD · K-REPLAY. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-POLYIA96, SRC-UCG156, SRC-RECON.

### PIA-154 · XIII.10 — Reusable agency factory

**Mandate.** Make specialized agents/machines composable from admitted atoms and grammars. The concierge returns machine, IR, interfaces, dependencies, refusals, witnesses and human projection. A specialized language engine is one deployment of this common factory.

**Acceptance.** Recompose the same kernel into one language specialist and one non-language computational service, each independently installable and verifiable.

**Continuity:** K-EVOLVE · K-SHIP · K-EVD · K-REPLAY. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-POLYIA96, SRC-UCG156, SRC-RECON.

### PIA-155 · XIII.11 — Release evidence and limitations

**Mandate.** Publish actual tests, command results, environment, package hashes, benchmark scope, unsupported capabilities and residual risks. Historical reported tests are labeled separately from fresh release verification. Document meaningful limits without burying the working result.

**Acceptance.** Release checker resolves every claimed fresh test to a real log/receipt and rejects claims based solely on inherited reports or planned commands.

**Continuity:** K-EVOLVE · K-SHIP · K-EVD · K-REPLAY. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-POLYIA96, SRC-UCG156, SRC-RECON.

### PIA-156 · XIII.12 — Evolution science charter

**Mandate.** Use VII/VIII to investigate synthesis and evidence-governed evolution as research subjects, with falsifiable questions and comparative methods. Infrastructure improvement and scientific discovery are related but separate outcomes.

**Acceptance.** Each charter has research objects, methods, open questions, measurable milestones, relation to I–VI/IX and publication criteria beyond merely shipping a service.

**Continuity:** K-EVOLVE · K-SHIP · K-EVD · K-REPLAY. **Source lineage:** SRC-OWNER-CURRENT, SRC-POLYIA96, SRC-UCG156, SRC-RECON.

## Continuity-key register

| Key | Meaning | Invariant |
|---|---|---|
| K-SRC | Custody | Original bytes, source lineage and citations remain resolvable. |
| K-AUTH | Authority | Effects follow actual standing grants and current owner decisions. |
| K-SEM | Semantics | Types, domains, interpretations and losses stay explicit. |
| K-STATE | State | Every admitted change has a typed guarded durable transition. |
| K-GUIDE | Guidance | Receipt, acknowledgement and actual application are distinct. |
| K-EVD | Evidence | Claims and completion bind actual evidence of the appropriate class. |
| K-REPLAY | Continuity | Historical state and captured bytes remain reconstructible. |
| K-GEN | Construction | Generated objects have declared rules, derivations and limits. |
| K-PATH | Composition | Typed joint premises and context survive every composed path. |
| K-COST | Cost | Budgets, complexity models and measured resource use are explicit. |
| K-EVOLVE | Evolution | New versions pass admission without erasing prior versions. |
| K-VIEW | Projection | Human and machine views reflect the same state; reads are pure. |
| K-COVER | Coverage | Preservation, cataloguing, formalization and verification are measured separately. |
| K-LANG | Language | Symbols, notation and linguistic relations retain their own domains. |
| K-SHIP | Release | Runnable production and real acceptance determine shipment. |
| K-FRONTIER | University | Finite commissioning supports continuing bounded scientific inquiry. |

## Mandatory acceptance families

`registry/acceptance.json` defines the finite acceptance program. It includes source custody and all inherited obligations; actual live service and process restart; authenticated scope/origin controls; guidance receipt/acknowledgement/application; produce/verify/accept with forged and corrupted evidence controls; exact mathematical identities and domain preservation; promoted grammar expansion plus separate semantic evidence; typed multi-input paths and refutations; native compiler and language/nonlanguage agency composition; non-LLM article/prompt intake; tool isolation; continuous experiments and versioned activation; Astra contracts; books/curriculum; operational recovery and university mandate.

For each family record command, environment, source/dependency lock, actual result/exit code, evidence class, produced bytes and digest, verifier identity, negative controls and limitations. Snapshot integrity is not scientific correctness. A self-check is not an independent oracle. A passed finite family is not a universal theorem. Retained historical tests are not fresh tests until reproduced.

## How to work through the live harness

1. Read the current state and pending guidance. Select a dependency-ready DODGE work contract under current authority and budget.
2. Construct the promised production in an isolated working area, preserving all source origins. Record limitations and proposed changes explicitly.
3. PRODUCE captures actual bytes and the applicable obligation versions. VERIFY executes a registered verifier of the appropriate evidence class. On failure, retain evidence and return to production or HOLD.
4. ACCEPT only a current verified production. A new production requires new verification. Create a source-linked checkpoint and update the machine-derived next work frontier.
5. Acknowledge guidance explicitly, apply only admitted actions, and let the owner/observer inspect the resulting revision. Acknowledged advice is not automatically fulfilled.
6. At a real blocker, retain precise source/access/evidence facts and continue independent authorized work. At finite commission acceptance, publish the certificate and activate the continuing university research mandate under its budgets.

## Completion contract and continuing mandate

Commissioning ends at verified finite acceptance, not at an arbitrary report boundary and not at a claim to have completed mathematics. The commissioned system continues under `docs/AUTOMATON_SCIENCE_UNIVERSITY.md`: develop forms, grammars, machine science, curricula, books, experiments and versioned improvements; retain null results and open questions; make all work inspectable and guidable.

Deliver a runnable release, actual service address, source/capability/evidence registries, tested client and interface, operational runbooks, clean-install verification, all source/books, a complete inherited disposition matrix and the next executable frontier. Report precisely what has been deployed, what has only been verified locally, what is still unsupported and which hypotheses remain open.
